speaker: Doctor
text:

Given the normal blood work and lack of specific lesion descriptions so far, have you noticed any non-healing sores, hard lumps, or rapidly growing bumps on your head, neck, or hands?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Findings - Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium; Full_Body_Skin_Exam: An erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders observed on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and on the left middle finger; Lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth; Regional_Lymph_Nodes: No palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis (Penile SCC) and Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Finger (Digital SCC). The biopsy showing nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitotic figures, combined with the clinical presentation of firm, crusted, non-healing plaques on the penis and finger in a heavy smoker, confirms malignancy. No further questions are needed.
